summary: Iter 38 — Verified queue chip + technical page mythbuster reasons + RF plain-English intro + onboarding wizard label. Backend queue/status shape, concurrency cap, and verdict-calibration v2 seeding all pass unit tests. Frontend: 13 mythbuster reasons render, rf-intro-explainer + YouTube embed (gkXX4h3qYm4) present at top of #random-forest, dashboard chip correctly hidden when idle, analyze-mode-section mounted, onboarding label code verified via source ('Pick at least 1 stock' / 'Continue with N stocks', no '0/3'). HOWEVER — major architectural finding: under 6-stock concurrent-burst load, GET /api/analysis/queue/status itself times out >30s because the single uvicorn worker's event loop is blocked by Claude JSON parsing in concurrent _create_analysis_impl tasks. The chip silently keeps its last status (never surfaces), so users get NO transparency in exactly the saturation scenario the chip was built for.

critical.issue: Endpoint becomes unresponsive (>30s read timeout) during 4-concurrent-analysis pipeline saturation. Single uvicorn worker's event loop is blocked by Claude/JSON-parsing in _create_analysis_impl. During my saturation test (6x hybrid /start) the chip-poll endpoint timed out on every single attempt for 25s, defeating the purpose of the live-queue-transparency feature.

minor.issue: is_busy threshold uses running >= capacity-1 (>=3 of 4) which is fine; but during the burst test capacity_seen could not be confirmed because every poll timed out — recommend either (a) running uvicorn with >=2 workers, (b) offloading Claude calls to a thread/process pool so the loop stays unblocked, or (c) returning a stale-but-fast counter via a cached background task.

integration_issues.flow: Queue chip live update during burst
integration_issues.issue: Because GET /queue/status times out under saturation (see backend critical), AnalysisQueueChip's silent catch keeps last state and the chip never appears to busy users. Code-level fallback works (no error toast), but the feature visibly under-delivers exactly when promised.

action_items: Fix queue/status responsiveness under load: move Claude calls to asyncio.to_thread or a process pool, or run uvicorn with workers>=2, so the lightweight /queue/status handler can be scheduled while pipeline is busy.
Optionally: serve /queue/status from an in-memory snapshot updated by a background task (every 1s) so reads are O(1) even when the loop is contended.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/analysis.py: _ANALYSIS_RUNNING / _ANALYSIS_QUEUED are mutated from coroutines without locks — fine on a single-worker asyncio loop but will produce wrong counters the moment uvicorn scales to multiple workers. Document this constraint or move counters into Redis/Mongo.
AnalysisQueueChip silent-catch is good UX but should still log to console at debug level so prod observability picks up the saturation pattern.
calibrate_verdict correctly seeds confidence_adjustments=[] + calibration_version='v2' on every code path (verified).

success_rate.backend: 75% (3/4 — saturation test failed because /queue/status itself stalled)
success_rate.frontend: 100% on the 4 testable items (technical mythbuster, RF intro+iframe, dashboard chip-idle, analyze-mode-section). Onboarding wizard label change verified via source-grep only — admin account is past wizard, fresh-user reproduction not attempted.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The /technical static blocks are all in place (mythbuster=13 reasons, rf-intro-explainer + youtube gkXX4h3qYm4, intro inside #random-forest). Dashboard chip hidden when idle. The OPEN BUG is /queue/status latency under load — once main agent fixes that, fire 6x hybrid /start, then poll /queue/status with timeout=3s and confirm <500ms p95 + visible chip in headless browser.
rca of the issue: Single uvicorn worker on the preview deployment + Claude API calls that block the asyncio loop during JSON streaming/parsing. While 4 _create_analysis_impl coroutines are mid-Claude-call, no other coroutine (including GET /queue/status) gets scheduled until one yields. Mitigations: (a) workers>=2, (b) wrap Claude SDK calls in asyncio.to_thread, (c) cache the queue snapshot in a 1-Hz background task and read O(1).
